title: Hospital Management System: ER Diagram & Normalization to 3NF
instructions: Design an ER diagram with at least 5 entities including Doctors, Patients, Appointments, and Bills. Normalize the tables to 3NF and prove no partial dependencies exist.
outline_steps: Step 1: Identify real-world entities and relationship cardinalities (1:M, M:N)
Step 2: Convert ER diagram into relational schemas with primary and foreign keys
Step 3: Test functional dependencies and demonstrate 2NF and 3NF decomposition
Step 4: Provide sample SQL DDL statements (CREATE TABLE with foreign key constraints)
key_references: Silberschatz, Korth, Sudarshan - Database System Concepts (Chapter 2 & 7)
Dr. Verma Class PPT Unit 2 Normalization

title: Producer-Consumer Problem using synchronized and wait/notify
instructions: Implement thread synchronization in Java for a bounded buffer producer-consumer model. Handle buffer overflow and underflow conditions using wait() and notifyAll().
outline_steps: Step 1: Define BoundedBuffer class with shared queue and capacity
Step 2: Implement synchronized produce() and consume() methods with wait()
Step 3: Create Producer and Consumer Runnable worker threads
Step 4: Demonstrate deadlock-free execution in main driver method
key_references: Herbert Schildt - Java: The Complete Reference (Chapter 11 Multi-threading)

title: Class Presentation: Deadlock Avoidance using Banker's Algorithm & Safety State Matrix
instructions: Prepare a 10-slide PowerPoint presentation with visual dry-run on 5 processes (P0-P4) and 3 resource types (A, B, C). Explain Need Matrix, Allocation Matrix, and Safe Sequence determination.
outline_steps: Slide 1-2: What is Deadlock & Coffman Conditions
Slide 3-5: Banker's Algorithm Data Structures (Available, Max, Allocation, Need)
Slide 6-8: Step-by-Step Trace of Safety Algorithm with numerical example
Slide 9-10: Resource Request Algorithm & Real-world OS comparison
key_references: Galvin, Silberschatz - Operating System Concepts (Chapter 8 Deadlocks)

title: Class Presentation: B-Tree vs B+ Tree Indexing in High-Throughput Databases
instructions: Explain balanced multi-way tree structures, differences between B-Tree and B+ Tree (leaves linked as linked-list for range queries), and performance in disk I/O.
outline_steps: Slide 1-3: Linear vs Index file scan disk I/O costs
Slide 4-6: B+ Tree internal node structure vs leaf node storage
Slide 7-8: Insert & Split operations with trace
Slide 9-10: Why MySQL InnoDB and PostgreSQL default to B+ Tree indexes
key_references: Database System Concepts Chapter 14 Indexing & Hashing
